How do you feel about cursing?

I realize that a lot of people are moving to this site because Reddit started to crack down posts which members felt infringed on their rights to free speech. That, and/or they're tired of people being in control of many popular subreddits.

I know that censorship is a big no-no. However, part of what turns me off of Reddit is how much cursing I see. I think I'd be lying if I said it doesn't offend me in the least bit. I'm not going to reprimand anyone for doing it, but I wouldn't be making the post if it didn't bug me to at least a small degree. I get that we should be able to say what we want, but the amount of foul language I see is almost ridiculous. It seems like people are just saying (typing) those things just because they can. Here's an example.

www.np.reddit.com/r/WTF/comments/2w6nrv/how_to_shit_your_pants_in_a_tree/coo255d?context=3

The title, fine. It doesn't bug me. I'm sure some people would be pretty scared if a bear was flying up the tree like that. The comment though, is that really necessary? You really felt so terrified by a soundless moving picture on the internet to talk like that? The end sums it up perfectly, "I'm just looking at a gif." Exactly, so I don't see the need for that reaction. It sounds like they're on an uncensored episode of "Damn Nature, You Scary!" Another thing is how prominent the word "cunt" is. Any time someone tells a story where there's a person being mildly abrasive, they're a cunt. I feel like people need to tone it down.

I think people need to be able to say what's on their mind, but I feel like there's a threshold where it's just unnecessary to talk like that. I made my own response because I wanted others opinions in general, but also to maybe get some opinions of what I'm thinking.
I'm apathetic. The people who care too much about cursing usually end up being the thin skinned "think of the children" types.

On Voat or in general? In general, I withhold from swearing around others unless the situation calls for it; usually when lesser words would sound weird and stand out. By myself, on the otherhand, I swear a lot since I don't take losing personals very... calmly. On Voat, it's the same way as how I speak to others IRL: if the situation calls for it, I'll swear.

When I hear/read others swear, though, I am almost completely unphased, since I see it as common language and my brain has adjusted accordingly. I do feel that, as with all words in language, swear words have their place, but they're not appropriate in some situations.

1. I fucking love it. Not cursing, expression. The more offended people seem to be by the word the amused I am. For example, for some reason people go ape-shit over cunt, but less so for pussy, and usually not at all over vagina. Strange.
  2. Let's not confuse "curse" words with oppressive labels. I'm still not offended by them, but they just suck.
  3. Never ever use replacement words for cursing. For example, fudge or freak instead of fuck. If you can't reword the sentence to avoid your replacement curse word, you're inarticulate and I will ridicule you internally. Also, I would rather you say nigga or even nigger instead of "N-word," which makes you sound like an asshat. The smart ones among us are capable of distinguishing between actually using a word and making reference to it.

Sometimes I will replace a swear word, using fudge instead of fuck for example, when I either forget where I am or suddenly see there is kids around or something. A good example is that where I am it is very icy, and I slipped on my driveway and the elementary school had recently let out so there were many kids around. It was a long drawn out "fuuuuuuuuudge". Any other time I would've cursed for a solid five minutes, but didn't want to around kids. So I got up, hobbled my way inside and let it out there, much to the amusement of my landlords.

I had a really interesting conversation with a work colleague about swearing the other day. The gist being a swear word is just a word, a string of letters. Is a swear word offensive because it is a swear word or because of the intent behind the word as it is used in a certain situation? If I hate someone and I call them a c*nt, is it less offensive if I call them an idiot even though behind the words my opinion of them is exactly the same?

I'm on the fence with swearing myself. I do swear and there are times when a well timed swear word will make my day. However I do censor myself in professional situations, in front of my children and certainly in front of my grandmother. What I'm not sure about is why I chose to censor. I can objectively see that they are just words but it's so trained into us from a young age that swearing is wrong. What I do hate is people that use swear words just to try and evoke a reaction or to appear edgy, it's just lazy and makes you look like a plonker.

Cursing and swearing have never added anything to any conversation, have never helped find a solution. But it's just distasteful,offensive, childish and useless.
I'm mostly bothered by people who swear constantly when not angered because I can't take them seriously.
I don't particularly care, just keep it away from professional environments. I personally limit myself in it's use only if to make it have more of an impact when I do use it.

Holy shit and god dammit. I fucking love cursing almost as much as I love to fuck cunts with my cock. People who curse tend to be more honest, less stressed, and a hell of a lot more fun to be around.

Chilling with friends and I stub my toe? I'll be swearing like a sailor. Even if I am just chilling with friends, I'll use it to emphasize what I am trying to explain. Or seeing something really cool as in "That was fucking awesome" and such.

Towards people in a judgemental or hurtful way, like trying to put them down? I avoid that. I don't constantly put people down or try to hurt them, but I see it happen a lot around me, and those people use swears to 'make their point' about someone, when really they are just being an ass.
